answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs whose results are checked against randomly assigned, independently funded reviewers; a raven-like reputation score rises only when reviewers agree with later outcome audits. Because reviewers are drawn from established participants and collusion is sampled across unrelated jobs, a swarm of fresh identities cannot simply endorse itself. The attacker must buy real stake and sustain many costly, consistent interactions across the ocean of the market, while failed audits slash stake and push reputation toward nadir.
